title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 1.

questions.question: Who was Solomon strengthened in his kingdom as the son of?
questions.correctAnswer: David
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:1 states that Solomon was the son of David and was strengthened in his kingdom.

questions.question: To whom did Solomon speak when he addressed all Israel?
options: The captains of thousands and hundreds, judges, and governors
questions.correctAnswer: The captains of thousands and hundreds, judges, and governors
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:2 says Solomon spoke to the captains of thousands and hundreds, judges, and governors of Israel.

questions.question: Where did Solomon and the congregation go to worship God?
questions.correctAnswer: Gibeon
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:3 specifies that Solomon and the congregation went to the high place at Gibeon where the tabernacle was.

questions.question: What was at Gibeon that Solomon and the congregation sought unto?
options: The tabernacle of the congregation made by Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The tabernacle of the congregation made by Moses
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:3 describes the tabernacle of the congregation of God which Moses had made in the wilderness.

questions.question: Where had David brought up the ark of God from?
questions.correctAnswer: Kirjathjearim
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:4 states that the ark of God was brought up by David from Kirjathjearim to the place he prepared.

questions.question: What did David prepare for the ark of God in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: A tent
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:4 mentions that David pitched a tent for the ark in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who made the brazen altar that Solomon placed before the tabernacle?
options: Bezaleel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur
questions.correctAnswer: Bezaleel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:5 identifies Bezaleel as the maker of the brazen altar Solomon set before the tabernacle.

questions.question: What did Solomon offer upon the brazen altar at the tabernacle?
questions.correctAnswer: A thousand burnt offerings
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:6 states Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings upon the brazen altar.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon went to Gibeon to offer sacrifices at the tabernacle.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:3 and 1:6 confirm Solomon went to Gibeon and offered burnt offerings at the tabernacle.

questions.question: True or False: The ark of God was still at the tabernacle at Gibeon when Solomon went there.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:4 explains that the ark was brought up by David to Jerusalem, not at Gibeon.

questions.question: What did Solomon do after he returned from the high place at Gibeon?
questions.correctAnswer: He reigned over Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:13 states Solomon came from Gibeon to Jerusalem and reigned over Israel.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 1, Solomon spoke to the captains of thousands and hundreds before going to Gibeon.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:2 shows Solomon spoke to these leaders before the events at Gibeon in verse 3.

questions.question: How many chariots did Solomon gather according to 2 Chronicles 1?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:14 states Solomon gathered 1400 chariots.

questions.question: Which came first in 2 Chronicles 1: Solomon offering burnt offerings at Gibeon, or Solomon gathering chariots and horsemen?
options: Solomon offering burnt offerings at Gibeon
Both happened at the same time
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon offering burnt offerings at Gibeon
questions.explanation: Offering burnt offerings at Gibeon (verse 6) occurs before gathering chariots (verse 14) in the chapter.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon's kingly wealth included silver, gold, and cedar trees in abundance.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:15 states Solomon made silver and gold as plenteous as stones, and cedar trees as abundant as sycomore trees.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How did God respond to Solomon's request for wisdom and knowledge in 2 Chronicles 1?
options: God granted him wisdom and knowledge and also gave him riches, wealth, and honour
God refused his request and gave him only riches
God gave him long life instead of wisdom
God made him a prophet instead of a king
questions.correctAnswer: God granted him wisdom and knowledge and also gave him riches, wealth, and honour
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:11-12 explain that because Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge, God granted it to him along with riches, wealth, and honour.

questions.question: What reason did God give for granting Solomon wisdom and knowledge according to 2 Chronicles 1:11?
options: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to judge God's people
Solomon asked for riches and honour
Solomon asked for his enemies' lives to be spared
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to judge God's people
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states that Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to judge the people over whom God made him king, and did not ask for riches, honour, or long life.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 1:10, why did Solomon request wisdom and knowledge from God?
options: So he could judge the great multitude of his people
So he could be wealthy and honored among kings
So he could defeat his enemies
So he could live a long life
questions.correctAnswer: So he could judge the great multitude of his people
questions.explanation: Verse 10 specifically says Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to 'go out and come in before this people' because the people were very many and needed just judgment.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 1:9 reveal about Solomon's view of the people over whom he was made king?
options: They were as numerous as the dust of the earth
They were few and easily managed
questions.correctAnswer: They were as numerous as the dust of the earth
questions.explanation: Verse 9 describes the people Solomon ruled as 'like the dust of the earth in multitude,' emphasizing their vast number.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 1:8 show Solomon’s attitude towards God’s mercy and his own kingship?
options: Solomon acknowledges God's mercy to his father David and recognizes his reign as a result
Solomon claims his kingship is due to his own strength
Solomon disregards God's mercy and trusts in military power
Solomon demands riches as a sign of God's favour
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon acknowledges God's mercy to his father David and recognizes his reign as a result
questions.explanation: Verse 8 records Solomon praising God’s mercy towards David and acknowledging that he now reigns in David’s place by God’s grace.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon asked God for riches and the life of his enemies during the night God appeared to him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:11 states Solomon did not ask for riches, wealth, honour, the life of his enemies, nor long life, but only wisdom and knowledge.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 1:7 tell us about how and when God appeared to Solomon?
options: God appeared to Solomon at night and invited him to ask for whatever he wanted
God appeared to Solomon in a dream during the day
God appeared in a cloud at the temple
God spoke to him through a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: God appeared to Solomon at night and invited him to ask for whatever he wanted
questions.explanation: Verse 7 clearly states that God appeared to Solomon at night and said, 'Ask what I shall give thee.'

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 1:12, what additional blessings did God promise Solomon besides wisdom and knowledge?
options: Riches, wealth, and honour such as no king before or after him would have
questions.correctAnswer: Riches, wealth, and honour such as no king before or after him would have
questions.explanation: Verse 12 promises Solomon riches, wealth, and honour unparalleled by any king before or after him, in addition to wisdom and knowledge.

questions.question: What lesson about humility can believers learn from Solomon’s prayer in 2 Chronicles 1:10?
options: Solomon humbly asked for wisdom to govern a great people rather than for personal gain
Solomon demanded to be the richest king
Solomon asked for a long life to enjoy his reign
Solomon sought power to defeat his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon humbly asked for wisdom to govern a great people rather than for personal gain
questions.explanation: In verse 10, Solomon’s request focuses on wisdom to lead justly rather than riches or power, demonstrating humility and prioritizing others’ needs.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 1:13 tell us about Solomon’s actions after returning from Gibeon?
options: He reigned over Israel from Jerusalem
He went to war with neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: He reigned over Israel from Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states Solomon came from Gibeon to Jerusalem and reigned over Israel, showing the establishment of his rule.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon offered only a few burnt offerings at the brazen altar before the LORD at Gibeon.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:6 tells us Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on the brazen altar, indicating a large and significant act of worship.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 1:5 tell us about the location of the brazen altar used by Solomon and the congregation?
options: It was placed before the tabernacle of the LORD
It was inside the temple Solomon built
It was in David’s tent in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It was placed before the tabernacle of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states the brazen altar made by Bezaleel was set before the tabernacle of the LORD, and Solomon and the congregation sought unto it.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 1:14 describe Solomon’s military resources?
options: He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen stationed in chariot cities and Jerusalem
He had no chariots but a large infantry
questions.correctAnswer: He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen stationed in chariot cities and Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 14 details Solomon’s military strength with 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen placed in chariot cities and Jerusalem.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 1:16-17 indicate about Solomon's trade relations?
options: He imported horses and linen yarn from Egypt and traded chariots and horses with Hittite and Syrian kings
He only traded with Israelite merchants
He refused to trade with foreign nations
He imported gold from India but no horses
questions.correctAnswer: He imported horses and linen yarn from Egypt and traded chariots and horses with Hittite and Syrian kings
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 explain Solomon’s merchants brought horses and linen yarn from Egypt, and they also supplied chariots and horses to the kings of the Hittites and Syria.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon's request for wisdom was motivated by selfish ambition rather than concern for his people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:10-11 shows Solomon’s request was for wisdom to judge the people well, demonstrating concern for their welfare, not selfish ambition.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 1.

questions.question: After returning from his journey to Gibeon, where did Solomon establish his reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:13 states Solomon came from Gibeon to Jerusalem and reigned over Israel there.

questions.question: How many chariots did Solomon gather during his reign according to 2 Chronicles 1?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:14 records Solomon had 1400 chariots.

questions.question: Solomon placed his horsemen in chariot cities and also kept some in which location?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says Solomon placed horsemen in chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem.

questions.question: What imagery does the text use to describe the abundance of silver and gold in Jerusalem during Solomon’s reign?
options: As plentiful as sand by the sea
As plentiful as stars in the sky
As plentiful as leaves in the forest
questions.correctAnswer: As plentiful as stones
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:15 states silver and gold were as plenteous as stones in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What tree does the text compare cedar trees to in terms of abundance?
questions.correctAnswer: Sycomore trees
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:15 compares cedar trees to sycomore trees in the vale for abundance.

questions.question: From which country did Solomon import horses and linen yarn?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:16 states Solomon had horses and linen yarn brought out of Egypt.

questions.question: What was the price of a chariot and a horse imported from Egypt according to this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: 600 and 150 shekels
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:17 specifies a chariot cost 600 shekels and a horse 150 shekels of silver.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 1, the horses imported through the king's merchants were also supplied to which groups?
options: Kings of the Hittites and kings of Syria
Kings of Babylon and kings of Egypt
Kings of Assyria and kings of Edom
Kings of Moab and kings of Ammon
questions.correctAnswer: Kings of the Hittites and kings of Syria
questions.explanation: Verse 17 says horses were brought for the kings of the Hittites and kings of Syria by the king's merchants.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the structure of Solomon’s prayer in this chapter where he asks for wisdom instead of riches or long life?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: Solomon’s prayer (2 Chronicles 1:10-11) shows chiasmus by contrasting what he did not ask for (riches, honor) with what he did ask (wisdom), highlighting the central theme.

questions.question: The Hebrew word for 'wisdom' (chokmah) emphasized in Solomon’s request primarily denotes what concept?
questions.correctAnswer: Skill in judgment and leadership
questions.explanation: The Hebrew chokmah, used in 2 Chronicles 1:10, focuses on wise discernment and ability to govern, matching Solomon’s request to judge God’s people well.

questions.question: Which earlier biblical promise to David does Solomon seek to confirm in his prayer?
options: God’s promise of an everlasting dynasty
God’s promise of a land flowing with milk and honey
God’s promise of a new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promise of an everlasting dynasty
questions.explanation: Solomon asks God to establish His promise to David (2 Chronicles 1:9), referring to the covenant of an eternal dynasty seen in 2 Samuel 7.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage is thematically connected to Solomon’s request for wisdom and God’s response in 2 Chronicles 1?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Kings 3:5-14
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:5-14 parallels this account in 2 Chronicles 1:7-12 where God appears to Solomon and grants him wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon’s accumulation of wealth and military power in this chapter fulfilled the promise God made when granting him wisdom.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: God promised Solomon wisdom and also riches, wealth, and honor beyond other kings (2 Chronicles 1:12), which Solomon’s wealth and military buildup demonstrate (verses 14-15).

questions.question: True or False: The tabernacle and the ark were both located at Gibeon during Solomon’s reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The tabernacle was at Gibeon (2 Chronicles 1:3), but the ark was brought by David to Jerusalem (verse 4), so they were not both at Gibeon.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 1 illustrate the theme of divine approval and legitimation of Solomon’s kingship?
options: Through God’s direct appearance and granting of wisdom to Solomon
Through military conquest recorded in the text
Through prophetic writings read in the assembly
Through Solomon’s building of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Through God’s direct appearance and granting of wisdom to Solomon
questions.explanation: God appearing to Solomon (2 Chronicles 1:7) and granting wisdom legitimizes Solomon’s reign as divinely approved.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by God when He appears to Solomon at night and offers to grant his request?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty
questions.explanation: God's appearance and offer to Solomon to ask what he desires reveals His sovereign authority over granting requests and directing the kingdom of Israel (2 Chronicles 1:7). This shows God’s control over human affairs.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 1:10, what was Solomon's primary motive in asking God for wisdom and knowledge?
options: To judge the great people of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: To judge the great people of Israel
questions.explanation: Solomon requested wisdom and knowledge specifically to govern and judge the vast people of Israel effectively (2 Chronicles 1:10), highlighting his desire for righteous leadership.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is emphasized by God's response to Solomon's request, especially given Solomon did not ask for wealth, honor, or long life?
options: God values humility and wisdom over material blessings
God only grants requests that benefit the nation
God punishes pride by withholding blessings
God prefers long life as the greatest gift
questions.correctAnswer: God values humility and wisdom over material blessings
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:11 shows God commends Solomon for seeking wisdom instead of selfish gains, teaching that God honors humility and spiritual discernment above riches or honor.

questions.question: How does Solomon’s gathering of chariots and horsemen (2 Chronicles 1:14) reflect the theological reality about human reliance and divine provision?
options: It indicates Solomon’s rejection of God’s protection
It shows the necessity of divine blessing on human strength
It portrays a purely militaristic kingdom without spiritual trust
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the necessity of divine blessing on human strength
questions.explanation: Solomon’s military preparations (2 Chronicles 1:14) demonstrate that while human effort is employed, ultimate success depends on God’s blessing, as established earlier in the chapter (verses 1, 7).

questions.question: What theological significance does the tabernacle at Gibeon hold in this chapter?
options: It was the place where Solomon was crowned king
It was the center of Israel’s worship before the temple
It was the site of David’s covenant with God
It was a pagan high place repurposed by Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: It was the center of Israel’s worship before the temple
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:3 explains that Solomon and the congregation went to the tabernacle at Gibeon, the meeting place of God’s presence before the temple was built, indicating continuity in worship and divine encounter.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by the fact that Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on the bronze altar before the LORD at the tabernacle (2 Chronicles 1:6)?
options: The necessity of sacrifice for atonement
The supremacy of David over Solomon
The rejection of the Mosaic Law
The irrelevance of worship in the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of sacrifice for atonement
questions.explanation: Solomon’s offering of many burnt offerings (2 Chronicles 1:6) underscores the ongoing need for sacrifice to maintain fellowship with God, pointing to the sacrificial system’s role in Israel’s sanctification.

questions.question: How does the combined account of Solomon’s prayer (2 Chronicles 1:8-10) and God’s promise (2 Chronicles 1:11-12) contribute to biblical theology about divine wisdom?
options: Wisdom is a gift given apart from obedience
Divine wisdom is granted only to kings
True wisdom is sought for the benefit of others and is rewarded by God
God’s promises are conditional on military success
questions.correctAnswer: True wisdom is sought for the benefit of others and is rewarded by God
questions.explanation: Together these verses show Solomon’s selfless request for wisdom to govern his people (1:8-10) and God’s gracious granting of wisdom along with wealth and honor (1:11-12), teaching that God rewards godly motives with abundant blessings.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in 2 Chronicles 1:12 where God promises Solomon unparalleled riches and honor?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence
questions.explanation: God’s promise to bless Solomon with wealth and honor (2 Chronicles 1:12) reveals His providential care in providing abundantly for the needs and purposes of His chosen king.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Solomon’s reign starting after his return from Gibeon (2 Chronicles 1:13) have with the broader redemptive story of Israel?
options: It marks the end of the monarchy in Israel
It signifies the fulfillment of God’s promise to David’s house
It shows Israel’s rejection of God’s covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the fulfillment of God’s promise to David’s house
questions.explanation: Solomon’s accession to the throne (2 Chronicles 1:13) fulfills God’s covenantal promise to David that his descendants would reign, advancing the redemptive storyline toward the Messianic kingdom (2 Sam 7:16).

questions.question: What is the theological implication of Solomon’s extensive wealth and resources described in 2 Chronicles 1:15-17 for understanding God’s blessings to His covenant people?
options: God’s blessings are only spiritual, not material
God’s covenant blessings can include material prosperity
Material wealth is a sign of human pride
God’s blessings are only for the priests
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant blessings can include material prosperity
questions.explanation: The abundant silver, gold, cedar, horses, and chariots in 1:15-17 show that God’s covenant blessings to Israel extend to material prosperity when they walk in His ways, affirming a holistic blessing.

questions.question: How does the presence of the ark in Jerusalem, as described in 2 Chronicles 1:4, typologically point forward to Christ in biblical theology?
options: The ark is a mere historical artifact with no typology
The ark symbolizes God’s presence, which is fully realized in Christ
The ark represents Israel’s political power
The ark is a symbol of human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: The ark symbolizes God’s presence, which is fully realized in Christ
questions.explanation: The ark in Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 1:4) represents God’s dwelling among His people, a type that finds fulfillment in Christ, the true tabernacle of God with men (John 1:14; Hebrews 9:11).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Solomon's wisdom was self-generated and not a divine gift. What does 2 Chronicles 1:7-12 teach about the origin of Solomon's wisdom?
options: Solomon's wisdom came from extensive education
Solomon’s wisdom was granted by God in response to prayer
Solomon inherited wisdom genetically from David
Solomon’s wisdom was a myth with no biblical basis
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon’s wisdom was granted by God in response to prayer
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:7-12 clearly states God appeared to Solomon and granted wisdom after Solomon asked for it, showing wisdom is a gift from God, not self-generated. This refutes sceptical claims denying divine origin.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is given by verses 5-6 and verse 11 regarding worship and the heart’s condition before God?
options: External rituals suffice regardless of the heart
Sacrificial worship is ineffective without a pure heart
God values the sincere heart that seeks wisdom over ritual alone
questions.correctAnswer: God values the sincere heart that seeks wisdom over ritual alone
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 describe Solomon’s sacrifices, while verse 11 praises Solomon’s heart in seeking wisdom rather than worldly gains. Together they teach that true worship combines external acts with sincere, humble desires.

questions.question: How does the description of Solomon’s merchants receiving linen yarn at a price from Egypt (2 Chronicles 1:16) reflect God’s providential ordering of international trade and peace?
options: It shows Israel’s dependence on pagan gods
It reflects God’s sovereign control over nations and commerce
It indicates Solomon’s idolatry with foreign goods
It reveals a rejection of God’s law on trade
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God’s sovereign control over nations and commerce
questions.explanation: The trade relations with Egypt (2 Chronicles 1:16) demonstrate God’s providential governance extending over nations, enabling peaceful commerce that benefits His covenant people.

questions.question: What theological teaching emerges from the combined facts in verses 2 and 13 about Solomon’s leadership over Israel?
options: Solomon’s reign was established without support from Israel’s leaders
Solomon’s kingship was recognized by Israel’s leaders and involved collaboration
Solomon ruled secretly without public knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon’s kingship was recognized by Israel’s leaders and involved collaboration
questions.explanation: Verse 2 depicts Solomon addressing Israel’s leaders, while verse 13 notes his reign began after returning from Gibeon, showing his leadership was public and involved cooperation with Israel’s governing officials.
